ctx.x: I don't remember, I don't know what it was. I was just so happy to see Billy and Joe Guy and, you know, I would like to know, I'm sure Vernon would know. But I've forgotten. But as I say all the good bands would come through. Hamp, he came through. The first time I heard Dinah Washington. She was with Hamp at this time. And they had another vocalist, Madeline Green. And very good band, and one saxophone player that I remember, I was working with him when I went into the army -- before, just before I went into the…

So I stayed in the army for quite awhile, and I started to -- Vernon tried to get me to stay in San Francisco but I didn't see any musical future there, you know, and so I had to get back to New York. So I went back to New York and I started -- I went to work with Slam Stewart, and Errol Gardner had just left Slam and Billy Taylor was the pianist. And it was Harold West, Slam Stewart, Billy Taylor and myself. We worked for quite a while, we did quite a bit of work, you know. And we lived on the street because…
